relatedSnapshot.title: Let the contact text box grow with longer messages
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

On a contact's Calls & Texts tab the box where a rep types a text is a single line. A longer message scrolls sideways out of view, so the rep can only see a fragment of what they are about to send. The box should grow as they type, up to a sensible height, and then scroll inside itself.

## Problem

A rep writing a follow-up text of a few sentences loses sight of the start of their message as soon as it is wider than the box. Reading it back before sending means scrolling the cursor left and right. Saved templates written over several lines are also flattened into one line when inserted, because the box cannot show line breaks.

## User experience

* The box starts at one line, as now.
* As the rep types, it grows one line at a time so the whole message stays visible, up to roughly seven lines.
* Beyond that it stops growing and scrolls inside itself, so the send and template controls never move off screen and the message history above keeps its space.
* Enter still sends. Shift+Enter starts a new line, matching the Conversations reply box.
* When a message is sent or the draft is cleared, the box shrinks back to one line.
* Inserting a saved template keeps its line breaks instead of replacing them with spaces, and the text goes out exactly as it appears in the box.

## What's included

* The contact record text box on the Calls & Texts tab grows and caps like the Conversations SMS reply box already does.
* Template insertion keeps line breaks.

Not included: the Conversations reply box (already behaves this way), email composers, and any change to how texts are sent, scheduled or recorded.

## Done when

- [ ] Typing a message longer than one line makes the box grow to fit, up to about seven lines.
- [ ] A message longer than that scrolls inside the box; the Send, template and Send later controls stay in place.
- [ ] Enter sends and Shift+Enter adds a new line.
- [ ] After sending, the box returns to a single line.
- [ ] A multi-line template is inserted with its line breaks and sends with them.
- [ ] Light and dark mode both look right, and the existing behaviour when texting is unavailable is unchanged.
- [ ] Browser QA covers the points above.

relatedSnapshot.title: Open inbound text alerts at the exact message
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

Authorize notification content in batches and let a rep open the exact inbound text, including an older message outside the first loaded page.

## Problem

Name 9 the latest thread message as a proxy can expose the wrong content, and adding a message target to the existing paginated query would break its cache and optimistic update behavior. A deep link must also avoid regressing read state or changing the sending line.

## Proposed fix

Add input-ordered server hydration plus a separate exact-message query, then merge and focus the real message bubble while preserving existing Conversations state ownership.

## What's included

* Up to 50 delivery IDs hydrated through the authenticated recipient's current membership, responsibility, strict features, visible thread, and exact-message content policy.
* Opaque denied and unavailable results with no cross-workspace distinction or content leak.
* A separate exact-message repository and tRPC query that preserves funding fields and the existing infinite-query key.
* Atomic `sel` and `message` URL state; normal navigation clears stale message targets.
* One-time focus, scroll, and visible highlight on the real message bubble, including older history.
* Visible-only 30-second polling, or 15 seconds while funding recovery is pending, and no hidden-tab polling.
* Hydration, tenancy, authorization, exact-query, URL, focus, polling, funding, and read-watermark tests.
* No custom Name 10 list or badge owner, production enablement, deployment, or pilot.

## Blocked by

* Priority 3: Deliver authorized inbound text alerts once.

## How it should work

Two identical hydration passes can later prove a stable authorized result. Missing, denied, redacted, stale-responsibility, and unavailable records expose no message content. The URL selects the SMS thread and exact message. The target query does not change the paginated query key. The actual bubble scrolls and focuses once per target; polling never refocuses it. The newest committed merged message owns the read watermark, so opening an older target cannot move it backward.

## Who can do what

Only the delivery's current authenticated recipient may hydrate it, and existing workspace, CRM record, content, and client-role rules still apply. The link grants no sending or reading permission beyond Conversations.

## What the user sees

An authorized result contains workspace, receiving line, permitted preview, time, and Open conversation. The destination highlights the exact message. Missing or unauthorized targets show one generic unavailable state. The existing composer, selected sender, loaded cards, deliberate unread state, and hidden-tab behavior stay intact.

## Done when

- [ ] Batch hydration preserves input order and returns safe allowed, denied, or unavailable results for every requested ID.
- [ ] Cross-workspace, foreign-recipient, client, banned, removed, reassigned, answered, redacted, and feature-off cases reveal no content.
- [ ] An older exact target outside page one renders once as the real bubble and receives one focus/scroll action.
- [ ] Existing infinite-query cache, funding recovery, read watermark, sender identity, normal selection, refresh, and hidden-tab behavior remain unchanged.

## Open questions

None: all required decisions are settled.

## Expected outcome

An authorized alert can safely open the exact inbound text without disturbing the surrounding conversation state.

## Implementation context

This is priority 4 of five under Notify the responsible rep when a client texts back. Preserve behavior delivered by Reply to texts and manage unread, Find calls and texts in Conversations, and the linear-time query contract from Conversations gets slower with the square of a workspace's call count. AI context.md contains the implementation handoff.

relatedSnapshot.title: Make the chat UI look nicer
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Current State

The chat UI is functional but basic (`/components/website-builder/chat-panel.tsx`):

* Simple message list
* Basic input textarea
* No visual polish
* Limited features

## What Needs to Be Done

1. **Improve visual design** using Vercel AI SDK components
2. **Add rich message formatting**:
   * Code blocks with syntax highlighting
   * File change indicators
   * Loading states
   * Error messages
3. **Enhance input area**:
   * Better textarea with auto-resize
   * Send button with loading state
   * Keyboard shortcuts (Name 11+Enter)
4. **Add chat features**:
   * Message timestamps
   * Copy code button
   * Regenerate response
   * Clear chat option

## Design Inspiration

Reference: <url>

**Vercel AI Elements to use**:

* Message component with avatar
* Code block with copy button
* Streaming indicators
* Thinking/reasoning display
* Markdown rendering

## Component Structure

```tsx
// Enhanced message component
<Message>
  <Avatar role={message.role} />
  <Content>
    <Header>
      <Role>{message.role}</Role>
      <Timestamp>{message.timestamp}</Timestamp>
    </Header>
    <Body>
      <Markdown>{message.content}</Markdown>
      {message.code && <CodeBlock />}
    </Body>
    <Actions>
      <CopyButton />
      <RegenerateButton />
    </Actions>
  </Content>
</Message>

// Enhanced input
<ChatInput>
  <Textarea 
    placeholder="Ask me to modify your website..."
    onKeyDown={handleKeyDown}
    autoResize
  />
  <Actions>
    <AttachButton />
    <SendButton loading={isLoading} />
  </Actions>
</ChatInput>
```

## Visual Improvements

1. **Message Styling**:
   * User messages: Right-aligned, colored background
   * Assistant messages: Left-aligned with avatar
   * System messages: Centered, muted
   * Code operations: Special formatting
2. **Animations**:
   * Smooth message appearance
   * Typing indicator
   * Loading skeleton
   * Smooth scroll to bottom
3. **Responsive Design**:
   * Mobile-friendly layout
   * Collapsible on small screens
   * Touch-friendly buttons

## Features to Add

* **Quick Actions**: Buttons for common requests
  * "Change colors"
  * "Update text"
  * "Add section"
  * "Deploy site"
* **Context Awareness**: Show current website state
  * "Name 1 generated successfully"
  * "Last updated 2 minutes ago"
  * "3 files changed"
* **Error Handling**: Clear error messages
  * Retry buttons
  * Helpful suggestions
  * Contact support link

## Implementation Steps

1. Install AI SDK UI components
2. Replace basic message list with enhanced components
3. Add markdown and code highlighting
4. Implement message actions
5. Enhance input area
6. Add animations and transitions
7. Test on mobile devices

## Files to Modify

* `/components/website-builder/chat-panel.tsx` - Main chat component
* Create: `/components/website-builder/chat-message.tsx`
* Create: `/components/website-builder/chat-input.tsx`
* Add styles or use Tailwind classes

## Success Criteria

* Professional, polished appearance
* Smooth interactions and animations
* Clear visual hierarchy
* Mobile responsive
* Improved user satisfaction
* Feature parity with competitors (Lovable, Bolt)

relatedSnapshot.title: Format emails, write long texts and see scheduled messages in Conversations
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

In Conversations, reps can format emails the way they do in Gmail and write long texts in a box that grows or opens larger. They can also see and cancel their scheduled emails and texts right in the conversation.

## Problem

* The Conversations email box is plain text: no bold, lists, links or text size.
* The text box is three lines tall, so long texts are hard to write and check.
* A scheduled email or text only shows on the separate Scheduled page. A rep reading the thread cannot see that something is about to go out, or stop it.

## User experience

**Email**

* A formatting bar sits under the email text, in Gmail's order:
  * undo, redo
  * text size (Small, Normal, Large, Huge)
  * bold, italic, underline, strikethrough
  * text colour, link
  * numbered and bulleted lists, quote, align, clear formatting
* When the composer is narrow, the least-used controls fold into More.
* A Formatting button hides or shows the bar.
* The full email editor has the same bar, and formatting carries between the two.
* Usual shortcuts work: ⌘B, ⌘I, ⌘U, and ⌘K for a link.

**Texts**

* The text box grows with the message up to about a third of the screen, then scrolls.
* The expand button opens a larger editor with the same draft.
* The counter explains segments in words, including when an emoji makes the text cost more.
* Texts stay plain text: there is no bold or italic on texts.

**Scheduled messages**

* Each scheduled email or text for this person shows after the newest message, with a dashed outline. It shows who scheduled it, the message and when it will send.
* Cancel send appears only while it can still be cancelled.
* A message that is already sending, or being checked, says so in words.
* A failed one shows the reason.

## What's included

* The Conversations email composer (docked and full editor) and the Conversations text composer.
* Scheduled messages on the person's thread. They follow the same visibility rules as the Scheduled page, plus access to that person.
* Tracking: send events record whether the email was formatted, and cancelling from the thread is tracked.

Not included:

* email attachments (ENG-13827, the next PR)
* editing or retrying a scheduled message (ENG-14176)
* the scheduled count on the Scheduled button (ENG-14171)
* the record page's text box
* bold or italic in texts

## How it should work

* Email formatting is kept when the email is sent. The same formatting shows in the thread, in light and dark mode, including italics.
* Only simple formatting is kept: size, colour from the bar's palette, and alignment. Styles pasted from other emails do not change how received mail looks.
* Signatures (ENG-13828), merge variables (ENG-13831), templates and replies keep working with the formatted editor.
* A saved draft reopens with its formatting. Older plain drafts still open.
* Texts warn before the 1,600-character limit, and Send is disabled above it.

## Who can do what

* A rep sees a scheduled message on a thread only if they could see it on the Scheduled page and can open that person.
* Only people allowed to cancel it on the Scheduled page can cancel it from the thread.

## Done when

* A formatted email (bold, italic, list, link, size, colour) arrives formatted in Gmail and Outlook, and shows the same in the thread in light and dark mode.
* Signatures, variables, templates and replies still work, and send once.
* A long text grows and scrolls, opens in the larger editor, and sends the same draft.
* A scheduled message shows on the thread and can be cancelled there. A message that has started sending cannot be cancelled and says why.
* A rep cannot see scheduled messages they would not see on the Scheduled page, or for a person they cannot access.
* Tracking events are confirmed landing in PostHog from the preview.
* QA runs on a preview workspace with test mailboxes. No production sends.

## Design

Kit (full design): `#/screen/crm-conversations`, composer design pass of 29 Sep 2026. Screenshots are attached to this ticket. The production cut hides Edit and Retry on scheduled messages (ENG-14176).

## Implementation context

This is high risk: it changes outbound email content, the shared email display policy, and adds a new person-scoped read of scheduled messages. The scheduled-messages part is the slice of ENG-14168 that does not need its events read.

Full point-in-time context: AI context.md.

relatedSnapshot.title: Record every text message the platform sends
relatedSnapshot.description:
> **Context.** Glossary: master ticket ENG-12250. For THIS ticket: we have a messages table (`crm_message`) that stores text messages. **Every row in it today came from a message somebody sent to us.** Nothing we send is ever saved there. Sent texts only produce a line on the activity timeline, and texts sent by an automation produce nothing at all, not even a row in the database. Why it matters: our sales team sends 3,500 to 5,000 texts a day and we keep no history of any of them. Name 12 also wants texts counted as a sign that a rep is actively working a lead, which decides whether that lead can be handed to an SDR. That rule cannot exist while sent texts are missing.

**Size:** L · **Design:** none · **Blocked by:** nothing · **MVP****
****How it should work (Close reference):** <url>

### Overview

After this ticket, every text the platform sends is saved with the message provider's own id and the name of the rep who sent it, exactly like received texts already are. Automated texts are saved too, marked as automated.

### Problem

Five separate holes:

1. **Sent texts are never written to** `crm_message`**.** `apps/web/trpc/routers/sms.ts:104-123` writes only a timeline event.
2. `crm_message` **has no rep column at all.** No user id, no sender, nothing. Confirmed against the migration history. So even received texts cannot be attributed beyond "the rep who owns that phone line".
3. **The provider's message id is thrown away.** `sms.ts:138` returns it to the browser and discards it. The knock-on effect: Sendblue sends us a delivery confirmation webhook that looks the message up by that id (`apps/web/app/api/webhooks/sendblue/outbound/route.ts`), and because no sent message ever carries one, **that webhook matches zero rows every single time it fires.**
4. **Three automated send paths write nothing whatsoever**: `apps/web/plugins/workflows/sms/steps/send-message.ts:100`, `apps/web/plugins/workflows/sendblue/steps/send-message.ts:151`, `apps/web/plugins/workflows/phone-numbers/steps/send-sms.ts:94`.
5. **One send path skips the provider router entirely.** The `sendSms` procedure in `apps/web/trpc/routers/phone-numbers.ts` (line 1770) calls the Twilio service directly on line 1788, so a text from a Sendblue line sent through that procedure goes out of the wrong account. **→ Split out to** ENG-12301**. Not delivered by this ticket.** (The `:1979` cited here originally is `validatePhoneNumber`, ~200 lines away — corrected 2026-08-05.)

Also, the timeline event does not record which provider sent the message, so Twilio text messages and Sendblue iMessages cannot be told apart afterwards.

### Solution

* Add a sender column to `crm_message` for the rep, plus a flag or source field marking automated sends. **Agree the exact shape with A6 (**ENG-12252) so there is one convention, not two. Whichever ticket starts first writes it down.
* Write a `crm_message` row on every send, from **one shared place**, storing the provider's message id, the provider name, and the message type (text message versus iMessage).
* Route the three automation steps through that same shared place, so there is exactly one way a text leaves the platform. **The direct-Twilio procedure (**`phoneNumbers.sendSms`**) is split out to** ENG-12301 — its provider-routing half has since been absorbed by PR #5895, leaving only the recording half there.
* Remove the rule that skips recording when the text has no contact attached (`sms.ts:104`). Record it against the phone number instead.
* Confirm the Sendblue delivery webhook now finds and updates the right message.

### Scope

* In: the sender and automation columns, one shared send-and-record path, **four of the** **five** send routes moved onto it (the fifth, `phoneNumbers.sendSms`, is ENG-12301), provider and message type recorded, delivery webhook verified working.
* Out of scope: counting texts on a manager screen (B6), opt-out handling (C3), scheduling (C4), WhatsApp (not supported at all).

### Acceptance criteria

1. A text sent from a contact record creates a message row with the provider's id, the sending rep, the provider name, and whether it went as a text message or an iMessage.
2. A text sent by an automation creates a message row marked as automated, with no rep credited.
3. A text sent to a number with no contact record still creates a message row.
4. The Sendblue delivery confirmation webhook updates the matching message. Verified against a real send, not a unit test alone. **⚠ Verified in code only as of PR #5900** — a real send needs live Sendblue credentials, a handset and a publicly reachable webhook, so the PR asks for this to be read as "verified-in-code but not verified-in-production". Do not close this ticket as fully met until that production check has actually been run.
5. Sending from a Sendblue line goes out through Sendblue regardless of which screen or procedure was used. **→ Split out to** ENG-12301 **(blocked by** ENG-12263**). Not delivered by this ticket.** Criterion kept here for history; see the comments for why.
6. Counting "texts sent by this rep today, excluding automated ones" is a single query.

### Design (Name 13)

Backend ticket — for reference, where recorded texts render: 12 · contact record — calls & texts (mixed SMS + call log with delivery state) and 38 · conversations — call thread. Full screen map on master ENG-12250.

relatedSnapshot.title: CRM v2 Conversations: one composer for notes, texts and emails
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

The v2 Conversations thread gets one composer with Note, Text, Email and Call modes, so a rep can reply by email in thread, text a person who has no text thread yet, leave a note, or start a call without leaving the inbox.

## Problem

After the first v2 Conversations step, the composer sends texts only, and only to people who already have a text thread. Email replies still open a separate modal, and notes live on the record page.

## User experience

* Mode switch: Note, Text, Email, Call.
* Note saves to the person and appears on the timeline once it falls inside the loaded history.
* Text uses the existing reply when a thread exists, or starts a new text when it doesn't.
* Email: From is one of the rep's own connected mailboxes; To, Cc, Name 14 and Subject; Expand to the full editor; drafts save. Email bubbles gain Reply, Reply all and Forward.
* Call starts the dialler.
* Templates for texts and emails, Schedule send, and a Compose button to start a new conversation from the list.
* Calls in the thread gain outcome editing (reusing the call outcome picker), and text bubbles gain Save as note.

## What's included

* A permission-aware email-detail read for replies: provider message ID, reply headers, full recipients and attachment metadata, hidden from reps without email-content access.
* Real sends only through existing send paths.
* Starting a new text needs the same contact-access check as the reply path before it is used here (see the "Start a new text" follow-up).
* Not included: Attach, merge variables that fill in, Remind if no reply, Log a call, signatures per mailbox (each has its own ticket).

## Blocked by

* ENG-14165 (the v2 Conversations screen).

## Done when

* A rep can send a note, text and email from the thread, and each appears on the timeline after sending.
* Email reply stays in the provider thread with correct headers and recipients.
* A rep without email-content access cannot read bodies, headers or attachment details through the new read.
* Templates and Schedule send work from the composer.
* QA uses a preview workspace and a test mailbox; no production sends.

## Design

* Design (full kit): Acquisity v2 Kit, Conversations, route `#/screen/crm-conversations`.
* Production cut: see ENG-14165. This ticket un-gates the composer parts marked for it.
* The design artifacts are private until James shares them.

## Implementation context

High risk: a new email-detail read and real outbound mail. Builds on ENG-13830 (templates) and sits next to ENG-13831 (variables), ENG-13828 (signatures) and ENG-12968 (scheduling).

relatedSnapshot.title: Scheduled messages in Conversations: Scheduled folder, edit or retry, remind if no reply, better Schedule send
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

Scheduling, cancelling and sending already work. This ticket brings the UI up to the CRM kit design and adds one new feature, **Remind if no reply**.

* **UI:** the thread's dashed scheduled bubble gets Edit and Retry. The composer's bottom bar and the **Schedule send** panel get the kit's quick presets, the person's local time and proper date and time pickers.
* **Scheduled folder:** the Clock button next to Compose opens a Scheduled folder inside Conversations. It replaces today's separate Scheduled messages page.
* **New:** Remind if no reply.

## Problem

Acquisity/Acquisity#6705 (ENG-14469) shipped on 29 Sep. Scheduled messages now show on the thread as dashed "ghost" bubbles with Cancel send. What's still missing:

* **Edit and Retry.** To change a scheduled message, a rep has to cancel it and schedule it again. A failed one has no retry.
* **Remind if no reply.** Reps track follow-ups from memory or add tasks by hand.
* **Scheduling is slow.** Send later is the browser's plain date and time boxes. It has no quick choices, and it doesn't show the person's local time.
* **The Scheduled page is hard to use.** The Clock button leaves Conversations for a separate page with six status toggles (including "Unknown"), raw phone numbers instead of names, no message text, no link back to the conversation, and a lot of empty space.

## User experience

**Scheduled message on the thread** (screenshots 1, 2, 10 and 11)

* The dashed ghost bubble shows:
  * the channel and who scheduled it
  * the subject (email only), the message and any files
  * "Sends tomorrow at 09:00 · not sent yet"
* Pending: **Edit** and **Cancel send**. Cancel is already built.
* **Edit** opens the same Send later panel with the message editable (screenshots 3 and 4). The rep can change the text, pick a preset or a custom date and time, then **Save changes**. The ghost updates in place.
* Failed: the reason in red ("Did not send. The number opted out of texts on 12 Sep."), plus **Retry** and **Edit** (screenshots 7 and 8).
* Cancelled and Sent: a status pill, no actions (screenshots 6 and 9).

**Scheduled folder** (screenshots 18 to 22 and 26)

* The Clock button (with its count) turns the conversation list into **Scheduled**. The open thread stays on the right, and Back returns to the list.
* Header: Back, "Scheduled" with an orange "6 upcoming" pill, and Mine / Everyone. Below it are tabs for **Upcoming**, **Failed** (red count), **Sent** and **Cancelled**, then a channel menu and a search box.
  * "Sending" shows as a pill on its row, not as a tab.
  * "Unknown" is not a tab. Those rows sit in Upcoming with a "Checking whether it sent" pill.
* Rows are grouped under sticky day headings (Today, Tomorrow, Mon 22 Sep). Upcoming is soonest first, the other tabs newest first.
* Each row shows:
  * the send time
  * the person's avatar with a blue email or purple text mark
  * their name
  * the subject and first line of the message, plus any files
  * who scheduled it ("You" or the rep's coloured initials)
* On hover or keyboard focus, a row shows **Edit** and **Cancel**; touch shows them always. Failed rows always show the reason, plus **Retry** when retrying can work.
* Clicking a row opens that person's thread with its dashed scheduled bubble.
* The footer says the order and the timezone ("Name 19 first · Times in Asia/Dubai").
* The old `/crm/scheduled-messages` page redirects to this folder.

**Edit panel** (screenshots 23 to 25)

* An email opens **Edit scheduled email**: Subject, the message in the same formatting editor as the composer, then the time.
* A text opens **Edit scheduled text** with the plain box.
* **Date picker:** a white field showing "Mon 21 Sep" (or Today / Tomorrow). It opens quick chips (Today, Tomorrow, Next Monday) and a month grid. Today is ringed in blue, the chosen day is ink, past days are muted, and months slide as you page.
* **Time picker:** a white field showing "09:00". It opens 15-minute slots grouped Morning / Afternoon / Evening, each with the person's local time ("06:00 theirs"), and scrolls to the chosen time.
* The same pickers are used for **Pick a date and time** in Schedule send.

**Composer bottom bar** (screenshots 12 to 17)

* The bar runs along the bottom of the composer: **Remind if no reply** on the left, then **Schedule send** and **Send now** on the right.
* **Remind if no reply** opens a small menu: "Create a task if Name 20 does not reply", with Off, After 1 day, After 3 days and After 1 week.
  * Once set, the button reads "Remind in 3 days".
  * Notes don't show this control ("Notes never go to the contact").
* **Schedule send** opens the Send later panel:
  * presets with their exact times: In 1 hour, This evening, Tomorrow morning (the default), Monday morning, and Pick a date and time
  * the workspace timezone in the header
  * "Their local time is 09:30 local", with a **Use their timezone** button
  * a summary line ("Name 15 19 Sep, 09:00") beside Cancel and Schedule send
* The look should match the kit: spacing, icons, pills and the dashed ghost.

## What's included

* Edit and Retry on scheduled texts and emails in the Conversations thread.
* Remind if no reply on the Conversations text and email composers. This replaces ENG-14172, which is folded in here.
* The Schedule send panel upgrade, with the new date and time pickers, used for new schedules and for Edit.
* The Scheduled folder in Conversations, replacing the separate Scheduled messages page.

Not included:

* the scheduled count on the Scheduled button (ENG-14171)
* tasks, meetings and payments on the thread (ENG-14168)
* the record page composer
* AI SDR follow-ups

## Execution order

The second ticket cannot start until the first is merged, since it reuses the first ticket's Edit panel and Retry action.

### Wave 1: can start now

1. Edit, retry, Remind if no reply and a better Schedule send in Conversations: server canEdit/canRetry plus edit and retry mutations, the new date and time pickers, the rebuilt Send later panel wired into the thread's scheduled bubble, and Remind if no reply.

### Wave 2: starts once Wave 1 is merged

2. Scheduled folder in Conversations: blocked by the ticket above, whose Edit panel and Retry action the folder's rows reuse rather than duplicate.

## How it should work

* **Edit** is offered only while the message can still be changed: pending, and no send attempt has started. This is the same rule as Cancel. If it started sending in the meantime, say "Already sending, too late to change" and refresh the ghost.
* An edited message sends **once**, at the new time, with the new content. Edits still respect opt-out, contact hours and the 1,600-character text limit.
* **Retry** is offered only when the failure can succeed on a second try. Hide it for permanent failures like an opted-out number. Retry follows the send-once rules from ENG-12569, so a message is never sent twice.
* **Remind if no reply** creates a follow-up task for the sender at the chosen time, only if the person hasn't replied on any channel since the send. A reply before then cancels the reminder. It works for Send now and for Schedule send; for a scheduled message the clock starts when it actually sends.
* **Their local time** comes from the person's timezone. If it's unknown, hide the line and the button.
* Presets are worked out in the rep's timezone. After **Use their timezone**, they're worked out in the person's.

## Who can do what

* Edit and Retry follow the same permissions as Cancel. A rep can only change messages they could cancel on the Scheduled page, for people they can open.
* A reminder task belongs to the rep who sent the message.

## Done when

* A rep can edit the text and time of a pending scheduled text and email from the thread. It sends once, at the new time, with the new content.
* A failed scheduled message that can succeed can be retried once from the thread, without risk of a double send. A permanent failure shows no Retry.
* Remind if no reply creates the task only when there's no reply, and a reply cancels it.
* The Schedule send panel shows the presets, the person's local time and Use their timezone, and saves the right instant.
* Schedule send and Edit use the v2 date and time pickers. There are no browser date or time boxes left.
* The Clock button opens the Scheduled folder. It shows the right messages per tab, scope and channel, grouped by day. Edit, Cancel and Retry work from a row. The old page redirects to the folder.
* A rep sees only scheduled messages they could see on today's Scheduled page, and only message text they are allowed to read.
* The screens match the kit screenshots in light and dark.
* Tracking is confirmed landing in PostHog from the preview: edit, retry and reminder set.

## Decided

* **Editing a scheduled email (James, 30 Sep).** Since feat(crm-v2): format emails, write long texts and see scheduled messages in Conversations, emails have a formatting bar and a subject. The kit's Edit panel shows a plain text box. Editing an email uses the same formatting editor and can change the subject. Texts keep the plain box.
* **Retryable scheduled-message failures (Ebubeker Rexha, 30 Sep).** Retry is offered for failures that can succeed on a second try: provider_failed, internal_error, mailbox_disconnected, sender_unassigned, phone_funds_required, feature_revoked, membership_revoked. It is hidden for permanent failures: recipient_opted_out, recipient_blocked, recipient_contact_mismatch, reply_target_missing. Full reasoning recorded in the AI context on ENG-14517.

## Design

**CRM kit design (clickable): Acquisity v2 Kit, Conversations**

Click the **Clock button** next to Compose to open the Scheduled folder. Open these threads in the kit:

* Name 16: pending email, with Edit and Cancel send
* Name 18: failed text, with Retry
* Name 17: sent
* Any thread's composer: type a message to see Remind if no reply and Schedule send

The 26 attached screenshots show every state and menu.

## Implementation context

* Build on feat(crm-v2): format emails, write long texts and see scheduled messages in Conversations. It added:
  * the person-scoped read of scheduled messages
  * the `ScheduledGhost`
  * Cancel driven by the server's `canCancel`, which is true only while `attemptCount = 0`

  The production cut there hides Edit and Retry. This ticket turns them on.
* Add server-decided `canEdit` and `canRetry` beside `canCancel`, rather than working them out on the client.
* The current Send later popover is `components/crm/shared/send-later-popover.tsx`, used by `composer-text.tsx`, `composer-email.tsx` and `record-composer.tsx`. Upgrade it for Conversations without breaking the record composer.
* **Scheduled folder data.** Today's `crm.scheduledMessages.list` returns details only, with no message text, by design. The folder's rows show a subject and first line, so that text must pass the same person-access and content-visibility checks as `listForPerson`. Reuse those checks; don't loosen the list. Keep the list's live 10-second refresh for Upcoming.
* Replace `apps/web/app/(saas)/dashboard/(sidebar)/[organizationSlug]/crm/scheduled-messages/page.tsx` with a redirect to Conversations in Scheduled mode, and keep its `tool.opened` tracking on the folder.
* **Pickers.** Kit source: `kit/src/components/ui/date-time-picker.tsx` (`DatePicker`, `TimePicker`). In the app, replace the `type="date"` / `type="time"` inputs in `send-later-popover.tsx`. Keep the existing rules: times are worked out in the rep's zone, and texts can't be scheduled outside contact hours.
* Remind if no reply needs a delayed check (send time plus N), then a task if no inbound message on any channel since the send. Cancel it on reply.
* Relations: ENG-14469 (shipped base), ENG-12569 (send-once), ENG-13345 (cancel before execution).

relatedSnapshot.title: Show that a scheduled text is held for contact hours and when it will send
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

When a scheduled text is waiting for contact hours to open, the scheduled messages list says so and shows when it will go out, instead of showing a plain Pending past its scheduled time.

## Problem

Once texts can be held, a rep will see a message whose scheduled time has passed still marked Pending, with no explanation. That looks like a failure and invites a cancel and reschedule that is not needed.

## Proposed fix

The scheduled messages list recognises a held text and shows a Name 21 state with the time it will send and the reason, in the viewer's timezone with the zone shown, matching how scheduled times are already displayed. Cancel stays available on a held text.

## What's included

* The held state in the shared scheduled-message list components and the row.
* The list data carrying the release time and hold reason.
* Tests for the held row and for the transition back to Pending and then Sent.

Not included: any change to the hold itself, and any editing or rescheduling of a held text.

## Blocked by

* Hold a scheduled text that comes due outside contact hours until they open

## How it should work

* A pending text whose release time is in the future because of contact hours shows as Name 21, with "Sends at" and the time in the viewer's timezone.
* A pending text that has not yet reached its scheduled time shows as Pending, as today.
* A held text that is picked up and sent moves through Sending to Sent like any other.
* Cancelling a held text works exactly as cancelling a pending one.

## Who can do what

Same visibility as the scheduled messages list today: the creator sees their own, managers see what their team scope covers.

## What the user sees

A Name 21 badge on the row with the release time and a one-line reason such as "Outside contact hours for this contact". Hovering or expanding shows the contact's local time if known. Cancel remains on the row.

## Done when

- [ ] A held text shows as Name 21 with its release time in the viewer's timezone and the zone shown.
- [ ] A text not yet due still shows as Pending.
- [ ] A held text can be cancelled from the list.
- [ ] After the window opens and the text sends, the row shows Sent.
- [ ] Tests cover the held row and the state changes.

## Open questions

None: all required decisions are settled.

## Expected outcome

Reps can tell a held text from a stuck one at a glance and trust that it will go out.

## Implementation context

Fifth of five slices under Quiet hours: never call or text outside agreed times. Extends the components from Show scheduled-message states in reusable CRM components. Detailed planning is in AI context.md.
